'''Art Hobson''' (born November 27, 1934) is an American physicist and professor emeritus of physics at the [[University of Arkansas]]. He has written on the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], physics education for non-science students, and the social implications of physics.<ref name="uark-directory">{{cite web |title=Art Hobson |url=https://physics.uark.edu/directory/art-hobson.php |website=University of Arkansas Department of Physics |access-date=2026-09-23}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Hobson received a B.S. (1960) and a Ph.D. in theoretical physics (1964) from [[Kansas State University]], where his advisor was [[Boris Leaf]].<ref name="uark-resume">{{cite web |title=Resume |first=Art |last=Hobson |website=University of Arkansas |url=https://wordpressua.uark.edu/ahobson/resume/ |access-date=2026-09-23}}</ref> He joined the University of Arkansas physics faculty in 1964, became full professor in 1974, and retired in 1999.<ref name="uark-resume"/>

== Work ==
=== Quantum foundations ===
In a 2013 article in the ''[[American Journal of Physics]]'', Hobson argued that quantum phenomena are better understood as excitations of quantum fields than as particles.<ref name="hobson2013">{{cite journal |last=Hobson |first=Art |year=2013 |title=There Are No Particles, There Are Only Fields |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=81 |issue=3 |pages=211–223}}</ref> Physicists [[Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi]] and Michel Nauenberg published comments on the paper, and Hobson responded.<ref name="sassoli2013">{{cite journal |last=Sassoli de Bianchi |first=M. |year=2013 |title=Comment on 'There Are No Particles, There Are Only Fields' |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=81 |issue=9 |pages=707}}</ref><ref name="nauenberg2013">{{cite journal |last=Nauenberg |first=M. |year=2013 |title=Comment on 'There Are No Particles, There Are Only Fields' |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=81 |issue=9 |pages=708}}</ref><ref name="hobson2013response">{{cite journal |last=Hobson |first=A. |year=2013 |title=Response to M. S. de Bianchi and M. Nauenberg |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=81 |issue=9 |pages=709}}</ref> In 2018 he applied the same approach to the [[Schrödinger's cat]] problem.<ref name="hobson2018">{{cite journal |last=Hobson |first=Art |year=2018 |title=Review and Suggested Resolution of the Problem of Schrödinger's Cat |journal=Contemporary Physics |volume=59 |issue=1 |pages=16–30}}</ref>

=== Education and writing ===
Hobson developed "Physics and Human Affairs", a course for non-science majors, and wrote the textbook ''Physics: Concepts & Connections'' (first published 1995).<ref name="uark-about">{{cite web |title=About Art Hobson |website=University of Arkansas |url=https://wordpressua.uark.edu/ahobson/about-art/ |access-date=2026-09-23}}</ref> His popular book ''Tales of the Quantum'' (Oxford University Press, 2017) was reviewed in the ''American Journal of Physics''.<ref name="wheeler2017">{{cite journal |last=Wheeler |first=N. |year=2017 |title=Review of Tales of the Quantum |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=85 |issue=9 |page=722 |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article/85/9/722/1038409}}</ref> He has also written a column for the ''[[Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]''.<ref name="uark-about"/>

== Awards ==
He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1992<ref name="uark-directory"/> and received the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]]' Robert A. Millikan Medal in 2006.<ref name="millikan">{{cite web |title=Robert A. Millikan Medal — Award Winners |website=American Association of Physics Teachers |url=https://aapt.org/Programs/awards/millikan.cfm |access-date=2026-09-23}}</ref>

== Selected books ==
* ''Physics and Human Affairs'' (Wiley, 1982)
* ''Physics: Concepts & Connections'' (Pearson, 1995)
* ''Tales of the Quantum: Understanding Physics' Most Fundamental Theory'' (Oxford University Press, 2017)
* ''Fields and Their Quanta: Making Sense of Quantum Foundations'' (Springer, 2024)
